stories.title: International students and the UK job market
stories.summary: International students are encouraged to build skills and adaptability to improve employment prospects. Success depends on understanding recruitment timelines, sector entry routes, and immigration rules. Combining academic preparation with a clear view of the labour market is suggested to help students identify where their efforts matter most.

stories.title: Employability in the A-level curriculum
stories.summary: The Milburn Report highlights the need for sixth form colleges to focus on retention and positive outcomes for students. While academic education remains a priority, there is a call to integrate employability training into the curriculum. The challenge remains that students need jobs to be available for them.

stories.title: AI impact on graduate job markets
stories.summary: University graduates face global concerns regarding AI replacing entry-level roles. Companies like OpenAI and Google DeepMind are developing systems capable of performing complex intellectual tasks. A federal government report suggests that jobs involving cognitive work are currently the most at risk of being impacted by these technologies.

stories.title: Application strategies for study abroad
stories.summary: With over 1.2 million Indian students studying abroad in 2025, competition for international spots is rising. Changing immigration policies and regulations make the process increasingly complex. Experts suggest that a well-prepared application detailing academic interests and career goals is now essential for students to stand out among peers.

stories.title: MBA programmes and work experience requirements
stories.summary: Many MBA programmes now require significant professional experience, leaving graduates in a difficult position. Crummer Graduate School of Business at Rollins College offers a solution by accepting students who lack experience, provided they build professional skills while enrolled. The school aims to bridge the gap for young applicants.

stories.title: Oakridge Visakhapatnam ranked in national school list
stories.summary: Oakridge International School, Visakhapatnam, has been ranked ninth nationally in the International Day-cum-Boarding category by the EducationWorld India School Rankings 2026-27. The school also holds the top position in Andhra Pradesh and Visakhapatnam. These rankings are intended to serve as a national benchmark for educational excellence.

stories.title: Rodrigo Collaro on market development
stories.summary: Rodrigo Collaro of PATH Business and Marketing Solutions works to connect international institutions with the Brazilian market. His role involves building events and bringing new ideas to the education sector. He describes his focus as being relentless in pursuing business development and finding new ways to make connections.

stories.title: Kavita Sukhani shortlisted for principal award
stories.summary: Kavita Sukhani, principal of Oakridge International School Bengaluru, has been shortlisted for the Tes Awards for International Schools 2026. She is the only Indian school leader nominated in the category. The recognition highlights her commitment to academic growth and student wellbeing within the Nord Anglia Education network.

stories.title: Insights on education and future skills
stories.summary: Papri Chanda, a veteran education journalist at Hindustan Times Digital, oversees editorial coverage of policy and higher education. Her work involves managing newsroom priorities during exam cycles and policy announcements. She tracks how education systems are evolving to meet the demands of future skills and changing career opportunities.

stories.title: AI and the West Virginia job market
stories.summary: West Virginia students are evaluating how AI might shift future career paths as businesses adopt new technologies. Experts note that the state's unique industrial mix may lead to different outcomes compared to other regions. Local students are currently exploring technical training to prepare for a changing labor market.

stories.title: Catholic school weighs AI against academic honesty and human dignity - The Edwardsville Intelligencer
Filipino students win at Dubai ROBOlution 2026
stories.summary: The University of Baguio was named the overall champion at the ROBOlution 2026 robotics competition held in Dubai. Several other Philippine schools also received awards during the event. The competition brought together students to demonstrate their skills in robotics and engineering in the United Arab Emirates.

stories.title: Mongolian students receive Cambridge awards
stories.summary: Fifty-five students from 11 schools in Mongolia were honoured with Outstanding Cambridge Learner Awards. These students achieved top results in the 2026 Cambridge International examinations across more than 40 subjects. The awards recognize high performance both nationally and globally according to the Ministry of Education.

stories.title: Seven-year-old Moldovan student wins mental math title
stories.summary: Seven-year-old Ayisha Frumusachi-Ismail won the Level 2 Grand Champion trophy at the International Olympiad of Soroban and Mental Arithmetic in Amsterdam. She completed 140 exercises with time remaining to review her work. Her delegation secured ten medals in total.

stories.title: Nguyen Thi Ha Trang - A shining example of a "5 Good Student" at the national level, possessing 5 medals in the National
Student wins district swimming competition
stories.summary: Lahari, a Grade IV student at St George International School, secured first place in the S.Abhivkarshi Memorial District-Level Swimming Competition. The school management praised her dedication and performance. The chairman encouraged students to balance their academic pursuits with athletic activities to achieve success in multiple areas.

stories.title: Westminster Int’l School celebrates Cambridge High Achievers in prestigious ceremony - Daily Lead Pakistan
Teens win Constitution essay contest
stories.summary: Four high school students from Solano County received scholarships for their essays on the founding documents of the United States. The contest, organized by the Solano Constitution Discussion Group, awarded the title of Guardians of the Republic to students who provided the most compelling analysis of the republic.

stories.title: Two students from Telangana qualify for national aviation finals
stories.summary: Two students from Kasturba Gandhi Balika Vidyalaya have qualified for the National Aviation Olympiad finals. They were selected from a pool of 2.09 lakh participants across 12,400 schools. The national competition will feature 145 finalists in total.

stories.title: Former IBO medalist returns to Lam Son Gifted School as teacher
stories.summary: Nguyen Dac Hieu, a 2016 International Biology Olympiad bronze medalist, has returned to his alma mater, Lam Son High School for the Gifted, as a biology teacher. He is among 732 new recruits for public educational institutions in Thanh Hoa, starting his classroom tenure on November 1.

stories.title: Student tops national ITI automobile trade
stories.summary: Supriti Mahapatra, the daughter of an auto-rickshaw driver, has secured the top national position in the ITI Automobile trade. Scoring 99.5 per cent, she will be honoured by Prime Minister Narendra Modi at the upcoming Skill Convocation Ceremony on 21 November.

stories.title: WMO updates climate guidance for El Niño preparedness
stories.summary: The World Meteorological Organization is increasing support for its 194 members to manage El Niño and La Niña climate patterns. The agency uses quarterly and monthly updates to track fluctuating ocean temperatures in the Pacific, aiming to guide early action and preparedness for global climate shifts.

stories.title: Central Philippine University team wins regional math Olympiad
stories.summary: The Central Philippine University Electronics Engineering team secured the championship title at the 2026 Regional ECE Math Olympiad. The competition was organized by the local student chapter of the Institute of Electronics Engineers of the Philippines and held on 26 October 2026.

stories.title: Alphores institutions to hold state-level math Olympiad
stories.summary: Alphores Educational Institutions will conduct the Alphores Maths Olympiad Test on 6 and 15 December 2026 across Telangana. The organization plans to distribute 4,44,444 rupees in cash prizes on National Mathematics Day. Posters for the event were released by chairman V Narender Reddy.

stories.title: India to host first National Tribal Olympiad in December
stories.summary: The first National Tribal Olympiad is scheduled for 13 December 2026 for tribal students in Classes VI to X. The syllabus includes Adivasi history, heritage, and constitutional rights. Organizers report receiving over 1,500 applications after extending the deadline to 29 November 2026.

stories.title: National Tribal Olympiad workbook sees high demand
stories.summary: The first National Tribal Olympiad will take place in December, featuring questions on tribal heritage and achievers. Advisor Mahadev Toppo stated that the official workbook, containing 626 questions, is selling quickly as tribal communities prepare for the event. The initiative aims to inspire students to dream big.

stories.title: Turkmen university announces international philosophy and economics Olympiads
stories.summary: The International University for the Humanities and Development will host the third International Philosophy and Economics Olympiads from 7 to 11 December 2026. The online competitions are open to students from Turkmenistan and abroad, with no limit on the number of applicants per university.

stories.title: Guide for parents navigating the primary to secondary school transition
stories.summary: Moving to secondary school introduces academic and social changes, including larger campuses and increased responsibility. Experts suggest that parents can assist by encouraging independence and organization. A positive transition is intended to build the necessary skills for future learning and post-secondary education.

stories.title: Planning and execution gaps often drive missed deadlines
stories.summary: Timelines frequently slip despite teams having adequate resources and clear goals. According to recent analysis, projects often prove more complex during execution than anticipated during the planning phase. Decisions take longer than expected, and dependencies are often underestimated by those managing the work.

stories.title: Employment in the AI era: how schools can train students for future careers - South China Morning Post
How students use AI matters more than whether they use it - District Administration
Workshops in Macao aim to teach AI literacy
stories.summary: UNU Macau is hosting three workshops on 28 November to help teachers integrate AI into classrooms. The sessions cover questioning AI content and building machine learning models. Participants may apply for professional development credits, provided they meet attendance requirements and submit their applications before the event date.

stories.title: Survey finds teachers use AI without clear policies
stories.summary: A survey of Canadian teachers shows widespread use of AI for grading and creating assignments, often without formal guidelines. Students report that teachers frequently fail to disclose their use of the technology while simultaneously restricting student access. The classroom now has a double standard for automated work.

stories.title: Letter argues against penalising students for AI use
stories.summary: A correspondent suggests that penalising students for using AI tools is a failure of an education system that has not adapted to modern technology. The letter argues that AI is a permanent fixture and that threatening career prospects for its use is an inadequate response to technological change.

stories.title: Indiana nonprofit launches scholarship for college seniors
stories.summary: INvestEd has introduced a success scholarship offering up to 5,000 dollars to help rising juniors and seniors finish their degrees. The nonprofit intends to support at least 600 students annually. The award is designed as a last dollar payment for remaining financial needs.

stories.title: Borlaug scholarship offers funding for African PhD students
stories.summary: The NAPB Borlaug Scholars Africa Programme is accepting applications for six fully funded scholarships for doctoral students in plant breeding. The two-year program provides financial support, international exposure, and professional mentorship to researchers enrolled at African universities.

stories.title: Carson Boyle Memorial Scholarship continues legacy of supporting OSUIT students - news.okstate.edu
St. Louis scholarship program enters fourth year
stories.summary: The Michael O.D. Brown Memorial Scholarship is accepting applications from graduating seniors in St. Louis until 15 January 2027. Since its inception, the foundation has awarded 189,000 dollars in scholarships and 16,000 dollars in care packages to 63 students.

stories.title: Bursky School of Public Health launches scholarship program
stories.summary: The Bursky School of Public Health will award 100,000 dollar scholarships to 10 incoming Master of Public Health students each year starting in 2027. The funding covers tuition, living expenses, and a 5,000 dollar practicum stipend to reduce student debt.

stories.title: South Africa opens applications for teacher training bursary
stories.summary: The Funza Lushaka Bursary Scheme is accepting applications until 31 January 2027. The program provides financial aid to students pursuing teaching degrees in collaboration with the Department of Basic Education and the National Student Financial Aid Scheme.

stories.title: University of Warwick offers 80 fully funded research scholarships
stories.summary: The University of Warwick has opened its 2027 postgraduate research competition, offering up to 80 fully funded scholarships. The awards include tuition fees and tax-free stipends for successful applicants. The deadline for submissions is 10 December 2026.

stories.title: DAAD offers scholarships for Sub-Saharan African researchers
stories.summary: The German Academic Exchange Service is inviting applications for its 2026 In-Country and In-Region scholarship program. The initiative provides funding for Master's and doctoral studies to support research excellence and academic development across Sub-Saharan Africa.

stories.title: Airtel Africa Foundation opens technology scholarship applications
stories.summary: The Airtel Africa Foundation is offering 500,000 naira scholarships to 100 Nigerian undergraduates studying ICT courses. The initiative is part of a 100 million naira commitment to the Airtel Africa Tech Fellowship. Existing beneficiaries may also qualify for renewal.

stories.title: Madhya Pradesh Board announces college scholarship applications
stories.summary: The Madhya Pradesh Board of Secondary Education has opened applications for the Central Sector Scheme of Scholarship for the 2025-26 cycle. Students who passed the 2026 higher secondary examination with over 80 percentile marks are eligible to apply through the National Scholarship Portal.

stories.title: Oxford Saïd offers MBA scholarships
stories.summary: The University of Oxford Saïd Business School is offering MBA scholarships worth up to £40,000 for international students. The program aims to support candidates with exceptional leadership potential across business and government sectors. The scholarships are supported by philanthropist Wafic Saïd and the Saïd Foundation.

stories.title: Trinity College Dublin awards Chinese studies scholarships
stories.summary: Trinity College Dublin has awarded scholarships to students pursuing an M.Phil. in Chinese Studies. The awards, established by Dr. Jonathan KS Chiu and Dr. Margaret Sau-Sheung Ip, support students from China and Hong Kong. Other recipients were honored based on academic merit and financial need.

stories.title: IBPS PO mains results expected today
stories.summary: The Institute of Banking Personnel Selection is expected to release the results for the Probationary Officer mains examination by late evening today. Candidates can access their results through the official website at ibps.in once the link is activated.

stories.title: BPSC 72nd CCE prelims tentatively set for January
stories.summary: The Bihar Public Service Commission has announced a tentative date of January 17, 2027, for the 72nd Combined Competitive Examination preliminary test. The commission stated that detailed instructions will be published on its official website. The date remains subject to change.

stories.title: Maharashtra adds two BDS counselling rounds
stories.summary: The Maharashtra State Common Entrance Test Cell has announced two additional special stray vacancy rounds to fill 20 vacant Bachelor of Dental Surgery seats. The decision follows an extension of the admission cut-off date by the Medical Counselling Committee. Allotment results are scheduled for November 21 and 26.

stories.title: MAH MBA CET 2027 pattern revised
stories.summary: The Maharashtra State Common Entrance Test Cell has reduced the MBA and MMS CET 2027 examination to 150 questions and 150 marks. The duration has been shortened from 150 minutes to 120 minutes. The new format applies to all management entrance exams for the 2027-28 academic session.

stories.title: UP assistant teacher exam proceeds as planned
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh Education Service Selection Commission confirmed that the assistant teacher recruitment exam will be held on December 3 and 4. The commission is filing an FIR after a fake notice regarding the cancellation of the test circulated on social media.

stories.title: Allahabad High Court removes objection fee
stories.summary: The Allahabad High Court has invited objections against questions in the Private Secretary Grade-I recruitment exam. Candidates may submit challenges online until November 22. The court has removed the previous requirement to pay a fee of 500 rupees per objection. The fee has been eliminated.

stories.title: Maharashtra TET re-examination awaits government approval
stories.summary: The Maharashtra State Council of Examination plans to hold the cancelled Teacher Eligibility Test in early 2027. The examination was previously called off following reports of a question paper leak. The council is currently waiting for official state government approval to proceed.

stories.title: CHSE Odisha releases 2027 exam schedule
stories.summary: The Council of Higher Secondary Education Odisha has released its 2027 exam schedule. Theory examinations for Class 12 are set to begin on February 16 and conclude on March 31. Practical exams are scheduled to take place between January 4 and January 16.

stories.title: UPPSC PCS 2026 admit card release pending
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh Public Service Commission has not yet confirmed a release date for the PCS 2026 preliminary examination admit cards. Candidates are expected to download the documents from the official website ahead of the scheduled December 6 examination.

stories.title: SSC awaits result declaration for 2026 exams
stories.summary: The Staff Selection Commission has not yet announced a date for the release of the Stenographer Grade C and D or the Junior Hindi Translator Paper-I results. Candidates are advised to monitor the official website for updates on the recruitment process.

stories.title: West Bengal board exams may face delays
stories.summary: West Bengal Class 10 and 12 board examinations may be deferred by two weeks in 2027 due to the census exercise. Education Minister Dipak Barman stated that final dates will be determined after reviewing the census process and prevailing circumstances.

stories.title: WBCHSE to announce Class 12 semester results
stories.summary: The West Bengal Council of Higher Secondary Education will announce the Class 12 third semester results on November 27 at 2:30 pm. Students can access their results online from 3 pm using their roll and registration numbers.

stories.title: ATU Donegal estimates loss from visa refusals
stories.summary: Atlantic Technology University faces an estimated 420,000 euro loss due to international student visa refusals at its Donegal campuses. Across all campuses, 90 accepted applicants were unable to enroll, resulting in a total estimated loss of 1.2 million euro in tuition fees.

stories.title: Morocco to host 114 Zambian students
stories.summary: Morocco will host 114 Zambian students for university and technical studies during the 2026-2027 academic year. The scholarship program is part of an ongoing bilateral educational cooperation agreement between the two nations. Orientation for the students took place in Lusaka on November 6.

stories.title: UK independent HE sector impact highlighted in new report - StudyTravel Network
High Court overrules visa denials for Gaza students
stories.summary: The High Court has overruled a decision by the Minister for Justice to deny visas to 48 students from Gaza. The Department of Justice has since reversed its position. Senator Patricia Stephenson has called for an explanation regarding the initial denial of the visas.

stories.title: Canada considers international students as numbers
stories.summary: Canada is increasingly focused on study permit caps, financial requirements, and enrolment targets for international students. While these students are discussed as figures in immigration projections or sources of tuition revenue, the individuals navigating unfamiliar communities to pursue opportunities are often lost in the national conversation.

stories.title: Exchange students find Canadian kindness surprising
stories.summary: Rojda Turgay, an exchange student from Istanbul, was surprised by strangers wishing her a happy belated birthday in Kingston. The experience challenged her initial skepticism regarding Canada's reputation for kindness, as she encountered unsolicited well-wishes from people she barely knew during her first week on campus.

stories.title: NYU resumes CPT applications after court ruling
stories.summary: NYU will return to its longstanding guidelines for processing Curricular Practical Training requests following a court order that temporarily blocked federal restrictions. International students may once again seek authorization for off-campus internships, including those that do not fulfill specific graduation requirements.

stories.title: Saskatchewan tallies economic impact of international students
stories.summary: Saskatchewan has proclaimed November 16 to 20, 2026, as International Education Week, noting that over 9,000 students from 115 countries studied in the province last year. The government estimates these students contribute up to $700 million annually to the local economy through their spending.

stories.title: Germany sees drop in EU Blue Card issuance
stories.summary: Germany issued 56,252 EU Blue Cards in 2024, an 18.5 percent decline from the 68,997 issued in 2023. While Indian nationals remain the largest recipient group, the overall decrease in issuance across the European Union reflects a shifting landscape for skilled-worker migration.

stories.title: Hopkinton High sees spike in international students
stories.summary: An increase in international students at Hopkinton High School has been attributed to individuals routed from Masters Academy. The private school, which focuses on training elite young athletes, is currently undergoing a long comprehensive certification process for its 82-acre campus in Stow.

stories.title: Nepali families invest heavily in overseas education
stories.summary: Nepali families invested an estimated Rs 141 billion in overseas education during the 2025-26 academic year. While a student visa was once considered the finish line, the government suggests that students must now look beyond university acceptance to consider how their education enables career mobility.

stories.title: India overhauls visa framework to simplify travel
stories.summary: India is restructuring its visa regulations, collapsing 13 major categories into nine and reducing 49 subcategories to 23. The Ministry of Home Affairs aims to make travel seamless by reducing required fields on application forms by up to 70 percent, drawing from global standards.

stories.title: UDINUS students lead AI literacy campaign
stories.summary: Students from Dian Nuswantoro University held an educational campaign for 72 high school students in Semarang. The initiative focused on digital literacy and the ethics of artificial intelligence, encouraging younger generations to understand the risks and responsibilities associated with using the technology.

stories.title: Hanyang Cyber University rebrands AI program
stories.summary: Hanyang Cyber University is renaming its Sfumato School to the School of AI Convergence and Open Majors in 2027. The program requires multiple majors to help students build personalized careers, aiming to break down barriers between humanities and science through a foundation of artificial intelligence.

stories.title: Punjab Sets Start Date for AI Training of 25,898 Teachers
stories.summary: The provicial government of Punjab will train 25,898 public school teachers in Artificial Intelligence (AI) beginning November 23, as part of an effort to introduce modern technology in the education sector. The School Education Department is organising the programme in collaboration with PECTAA. AI focal persons from across the province

stories.title: Punjab to train 25,898 teachers in AI
stories.summary: The Punjab government will begin training 25,898 public school teachers in artificial intelligence on November 23. One teacher from every primary and elementary school will be selected to serve as an AI focal person, with the program delivered in five batches at the tehsil level.

stories.title: Grants fund AI tools for multilingual classrooms
stories.summary: Three teams will receive $350,000 each to develop AI tools for multilingual learners, with pilots planned in Colorado, Massachusetts, and Wisconsin. The grants, totaling over $1 million, address the fact that two-thirds of public school teachers currently have at least one multilingual learner in their class.

stories.title: Chicago schools face AI usage debate
stories.summary: The national debate over AI in K-12 schools has intensified after Google reportedly suggested that schools banning its AI technology could lose access to its search engine. The ultimatum creates a conflict for the Chicago school district, which has already phased out AI tools in the classroom.

stories.title: Korea partners with tech firms to train teachers
stories.summary: The Ministry of Education is partnering with Microsoft, Google, and Amazon Web Services to train 240 teachers in artificial intelligence. The program, running through December 5, aims to strengthen the skills of teacher research groups and officials in charge of convergence education.

stories.title: Handbook offers recommendations for inclusive education
stories.summary: A new handbook titled Inclusion in Action outlines recommendations for implementing the Right to Education, including engaging parents and providing equitable access. The guide draws on observations and interviews conducted across nine private schools in Delhi to suggest pathways for better integration and support for students.

stories.title: Principal reflects on Vietnamese education legacy
stories.summary: Nguyen Thi Minh Thuy, principal of Nguyen Sieu School, has been honoured as an Outstanding Teacher of the Year 2026. Her work continues a 35-year legacy of educational management in Hanoi, focusing on the potential for a purely Vietnamese school to provide a comprehensive education for local students.

stories.title: Dallas ISD to close six schools
stories.summary: The Dallas Independent School District is closing six schools following a decline in enrollment. The district currently faces a $128 million deficit after falling 3,099 students short of its initial projections for the current school year.

stories.title: School nurses call for measles prevention
stories.summary: The National Association of School Nurses has issued a call for increased measles prevention and response. The move follows the loss of the U.S. measles elimination status and a doubling of reported cases across the country.

stories.title: Academy trust to compensate children over badges
stories.summary: Lion Academy Trust will pay compensation to four children after a primary school threatened to refer them to the Prevent programme for wearing Palestine flag badges. The trust has issued a formal apology for the incident, which occurred during a non-uniform fundraising day in November 2023.

stories.title: Audits reveal infrastructure gaps in UP schools
stories.summary: The Cockroach Janta Party conducted social audits of 20 government schools across four districts in Uttar Pradesh. The inspections identified deficiencies in basic infrastructure, sanitation, and safety. The campaign aims to highlight the lack of fundamental facilities in state-run educational institutions.

stories.title: Alberta to revise school flag regulations
stories.summary: Alberta Education Minister Demetrios Nicolaides will revise a regulation requiring new outdoor flagpoles after school boards warned of million-dollar costs. The minister has advised boards to pause purchases, suggesting that funds would be better directed toward classrooms rather than new infrastructure.

stories.title: NMC proposes changes to foreign medical graduate rules
stories.summary: The National Medical Commission has proposed removing a requirement that foreign medical graduates be registered in the country where they earned their degree. The amendment aims to ease licensing rules for Indian students who pursue medical education overseas and intend to practise medicine upon their return.

stories.title: High costs impact medical school admissions
stories.summary: Tuition fees for Deemed Universities in India can reach up to ₹1.60 crore for an MBBS course, excluding living expenses. This financial burden has led to vacant seats, as affordability has become a primary factor in determining access to medical education alongside academic eligibility.

stories.title: NEP 2020 promotes multidisciplinary learning
stories.summary: The National Education Policy 2020 aims to move away from traditional subject silos in Indian higher education. By encouraging multidisciplinary study, the policy seeks to allow students to combine subjects and build diverse skill sets, marking a shift from the structured pathways of previous decades.

stories.title: Bar Council warns students to verify law colleges
stories.summary: The Bar Council of India has advised prospective students to verify the affiliation and approval status of law colleges before enrolling. The advisory follows a Supreme Court direction and warns institutions against making misleading claims regarding their legal authority to impart professional education.

stories.title: Migrant student faces barriers to school entry in Keralam
stories.summary: Arunima Mandal was initially denied admission to a private aided school in Keralam despite her siblings being enrolled. The school eventually admitted her on the condition that she repeat Class IX, citing concerns over the Class X pass percentage. The school prioritises its metrics over the student.

stories.title: National Medical Commission investigates ragging claims in Rajasthan
stories.summary: Freshers at Government Medical College in Banswara filed a complaint alleging sexual humiliation and threats from senior students. The National Medical Commission has demanded a point by point response within 24 hours, noting that simple denials will not suffice. The regulator expects more than a standard reply.

stories.title: Medical seats remain vacant despite high NEET competition
stories.summary: Over 3,000 MBBS seats remained unfilled following NEET-UG 2026 counselling, with 410 vacancies persisting in deemed universities after the final round. While government college seats were fully occupied, high fees in private institutions continue to influence seat utilisation. Competition is high, but affordability is not.

research.summary: A study of more than 10,000 college students found that exercising regularly may be more important for mental health than pushing yourself through intense or lengthy workouts.
